entries.definition: To cook food using dry heat in an oven.
examples: We baked a cake for her birthday.
Bake the bread until the crust turns golden.
entries.tip: Commonly used for bread, cakes, biscuits, and other foods cooked in an oven.
entries.breakdown: Baking usually uses an oven; it is different from frying food in a pan.

senses.definition: To cook food in an oven using dry heat.
senses.definitionZh: 利用烤箱中的干热烹调食物。
examples: She likes to bake cookies on weekends.
Bake the potatoes for forty minutes.

entries.definition: A place where people stay in temporary shelters; or to live outdoors in a tent or other temporary shelter.
examples: We set up camp beside the lake.
The children are going to camp in the forest.
entries.tip: “Go camping” is the common expression for taking a trip to stay outdoors in a tent.
entries.breakdown: Can refer to the temporary place itself or the activity of staying there.

senses.definition: A place where people stay in tents or temporary buildings, often outdoors.
senses.definitionZh: 人们在户外搭帐篷或临时建筑居住的地方；营地。
examples: The campsite has clean showers.
Their camp was near the river.

senses.definition: To stay outdoors in a tent or temporary shelter for a period of time.
senses.definitionZh: 在户外帐篷或临时住所中停留一段时间；露营。
examples: We camped in the mountains for two nights.
They camp beside the beach every summer.

entries.definition: An informal conversation; or to talk with someone in a friendly and relaxed way.
examples: We had a quick chat after class.
I like to chat with my neighbours.
entries.tip: “Chat” is informal. The past tense and past participle are “chatted”.
entries.breakdown: Usually describes relaxed conversation rather than a formal discussion.

senses.definition: An informal conversation between people.
senses.definitionZh: 人们之间轻松、非正式的交谈。
examples: Let's have a chat over coffee.
I had a friendly chat with my new colleague.

senses.definition: To talk to someone in a relaxed and informal way.
senses.definitionZh: 以轻松、非正式的方式与某人交谈。
examples: They chatted for an hour.
We often chat online after work.

entries.definition: To move upward using the hands and feet, or to go up something such as a hill or ladder; an act of climbing.
examples: The children climbed the tree carefully.
We climbed to the top of the hill.
entries.tip: Use climb a ladder or climb up a hill. The noun can refer to the activity or a difficult upward route.
entries.breakdown: Usually describes upward movement, whether by using the body or travelling along a rising route.

senses.definition: To move up or over something using the hands, feet, or body.
senses.definitionZh: 利用手、脚或身体向上移动或越过某物。
examples: The cat climbed onto the roof.
He climbed over the wall.

senses.definition: To increase or move to a higher level or position.
senses.definitionZh: 增加或移动到更高的水平或位置。
examples: Temperatures climbed during the afternoon.
The price of fuel continues to climb.

senses.definition: An act or journey involving movement upward, especially one that is difficult.
senses.definitionZh: 向上移动或攀登的过程，尤指较为困难的攀爬。
examples: The final climb was steep and tiring.
It is a long climb to the mountain shelter.

entries.definition: To make a picture or mark with a pen or pencil; to pull something toward you; or to cause people or things to come toward a place.
examples: She likes to draw animals.
Draw the curtains before you go to bed.
entries.tip: The past tense and past participle are “drew” and “drawn”. The word also has specialised meanings in sport and games.
entries.breakdown: A common verb with several meanings. Context distinguishes making an image, pulling, attracting, and selecting.

senses.definition: To create a picture or design using a pen, pencil, or another tool.
senses.definitionZh: 使用钢笔、铅笔或其他工具创作图画或设计。
examples: The student drew a map of the town.
Can you draw a simple flower?

senses.definition: To move something toward yourself or in a particular direction by pulling it.
senses.definitionZh: 通过拉动使某物朝自己或某个方向移动。
examples: Draw your chair closer to the table.
He drew the door open.

senses.definition: To attract attention, interest, or people toward something.
senses.definitionZh: 吸引注意力、兴趣或人们前往某处。
examples: The festival draws visitors from many countries.
Her talk drew a large audience.

entries.definition: Physical activity done to improve health or strength; a task done to develop a skill; or to use a right, power, or ability.
entries.definitionZh: 运动；锻炼；练习；行使（权利或权力）
examples: Regular exercise is good for your health.
Complete the exercise on page ten.
entries.tip: “Exercise” is usually uncountable when referring to physical activity, but a specific task can be “an exercise”.
entries.breakdown: Can mean physical training, a learning task, or the use of a right or skill.

senses.definition: Physical activity done to keep the body healthy or make it stronger.
senses.definitionZh: 为了保持身体健康或增强体能而进行的身体活动。
examples: Walking is a simple form of exercise.
She does exercise three times a week.

senses.definition: A task designed to help someone practise or develop a skill.
senses.definitionZh: 帮助某人练习或培养技能的任务。
examples: The teacher gave us a grammar exercise.
Try the listening exercise again.

senses.part: verb — use a right or ability
senses.definition: To use a right, power, or ability that you have.
senses.definitionZh: 使用自己拥有的权利、权力或能力。
examples: Citizens can exercise their right to vote.
The manager must exercise good judgement.

entries.definition: An animal that lives in water and breathes through gills; or to try to catch fish.
examples: We saw colourful fish in the aquarium.
They fish in the lake every weekend.
entries.tip: The usual plural is “fish”; “fishes” is sometimes used when referring to different species.
entries.breakdown: Can refer to the animal or the activity of catching fish.

senses.definition: An animal that lives in water, has gills, and usually has fins.
senses.definitionZh: 生活在水中、用鳃呼吸且通常有鳍的动物；鱼。
examples: A goldfish can live in a home aquarium.
Many fish live near coral reefs.

senses.definition: To try to catch fish, usually with a rod, line, net, or trap.
senses.definitionZh: 通常使用鱼竿、鱼线、渔网或陷阱尝试捕捉鱼类。
examples: My grandfather likes to fish by the river.
They went fishing early in the morning.

entries.definition: An area of land where flowers, plants, or vegetables are grown; or to work in such an area.
examples: She grows herbs in the garden.
My parents garden together every Sunday.
entries.tip: In British English, “garden” often means the outdoor area next to a home; American English often uses “yard” for this space.
entries.breakdown: Can refer to the planted area or the activity of caring for it.

senses.definition: An area near a house or in a public place where flowers, plants, or vegetables are grown.
senses.definitionZh: 在住宅附近或公共场所种植花卉、植物或蔬菜的区域；花园或菜园。
examples: The children played in the garden.
There is a small vegetable garden behind the house.

senses.definition: To grow and care for plants as an activity.
senses.definitionZh: 通过种植和照料植物进行园艺活动。
examples: She gardens to relax after work.
They garden together at the weekend.

entries.definition: A long walk in the countryside or mountains, usually for enjoyment or exercise; or to go on such a walk.
entries.definitionZh: 远足；徒步旅行；徒步行走
examples: We went on a hike through the forest.
They plan to hike up the mountain tomorrow.
entries.tip: A hike is usually longer or more challenging than an ordinary walk.
entries.breakdown: Usually refers to walking outdoors over a longer distance, often on natural trails.

senses.definition: A long walk, especially in the countryside or mountains, taken for enjoyment or exercise.
senses.definitionZh: 尤指在乡村或山区进行的长距离步行，通常为了休闲或锻炼；远足。
examples: The hike took us three hours.
We packed water and snacks for the hike.

senses.definition: To take a long walk in the countryside or mountains.
senses.definitionZh: 在乡村或山区进行长距离步行；徒步远足。
examples: They hiked along the coastal trail.
We hiked to a waterfall during the holiday.

entries.definition: To run slowly and steadily, usually for exercise; or a period of this activity.
entries.definitionZh: 慢跑；轻推；慢跑一段时间
examples: I jog around the park every morning.
A short jog helps me wake up.
entries.tip: The forms are jog, jogs, jogged, and jogging; the final consonant is doubled before -ed and -ing.
entries.breakdown: A jog is slower and less intense than a fast run.

senses.definition: To run at a slow, steady speed, especially as a form of exercise.
senses.definitionZh: 以缓慢、稳定的速度跑步，尤指作为一种锻炼方式；慢跑。
examples: She jogs for twenty minutes after work.
We jogged along the beach at sunrise.

senses.definition: A period of slow, steady running for exercise.
senses.definitionZh: 为了锻炼而进行的一段缓慢、稳定的跑步；慢跑。
examples: Let's go for a short jog.
He went for a jog before breakfast.

entries.definition: To make clothing or other items by joining loops of yarn with knitting needles; or a piece of knitted fabric.
examples: My aunt taught me to knit a scarf.
She knitted a warm hat for the baby.
entries.tip: The past tense is “knitted” or “knit”; “knitted” is common in everyday use.
entries.breakdown: Usually refers to making fabric by forming connected loops of yarn.

senses.definition: To make clothing or fabric by using needles to form connected loops of yarn.
senses.definitionZh: 使用织针将纱线编成相互连接的线圈，以制作衣物或织物。
examples: He learned to knit from his grandmother.
She knits socks during the winter.

senses.definition: A knitted piece of clothing or fabric.
senses.definitionZh: 针织制品或针织面料。
examples: The shop sells soft cotton knits.
This knit is warm but lightweight.

entries.definition: A coloured liquid or substance used to cover or decorate a surface; or to create a picture by applying it.
examples: We need more paint for the bedroom wall.
He likes to paint landscapes.
entries.tip: “Paint” can mean the material or the activity. A person who paints pictures is a painter.
entries.breakdown: Can describe decorating a surface or creating an image with coloured material.

senses.definition: A coloured liquid or substance spread over a surface to protect or decorate it.
senses.definitionZh: 涂在表面上以保护或装饰物体的有色液体或物质；油漆或颜料。
examples: The paint on the door is still wet.
We bought blue paint for the kitchen.

senses.definition: To cover a surface with paint.
senses.definitionZh: 在表面涂上颜料或油漆。
examples: They painted the fence white.
I painted my bedroom last weekend.

senses.definition: To create a picture by putting paint onto paper, canvas, or another surface.
senses.definitionZh: 通过将颜料涂在纸张、画布或其他表面上创作图画。
examples: She paints portraits of her friends.
The artist painted a view of the harbour.

entries.definition: A picture made using a camera; or to take a picture of someone or something with a camera.
examples: I found an old photograph of my grandparents.
The reporter photographed the event.
entries.tip: The noun is stressed on the first syllable. Related forms include photographer and photography.
entries.breakdown: The noun is the image; the verb is the action of recording an image with a camera.

senses.definition: A picture made by using a camera to record an image.
senses.definitionZh: 使用相机记录图像而形成的图片；照片。
examples: This photograph was taken in 1998.
She keeps a photograph of her family on her desk.

senses.definition: To take a picture of a person, place, or thing using a camera.
senses.definitionZh: 使用相机拍摄人物、地点或事物。
examples: The journalist photographed the crowd.
Visitors are allowed to photograph the building.

entries.definition: To do an activity repeatedly in order to improve a skill; or to carry out a profession or method regularly.
examples: You should practise speaking English every day.
She practises law in Kuala Lumpur.
entries.tip: British English uses “practise” as the verb and “practice” as the noun. American English uses “practice” for both.
entries.breakdown: Repeated action helps improve ability; the verb can also mean to work in a profession.

senses.definition: To repeat an activity regularly so that you become better at it.
senses.definitionZh: 定期重复某项活动，以提高自己的能力。
examples: He practises the piano every evening.
We need to practise for the presentation.

senses.definition: To work in a profession or regularly use a particular method or belief.
senses.definitionZh: 从事某种职业，或定期采用某种方法或信念。
examples: She practises medicine in a local clinic.
They practise meditation each morning.

entries.definition: To look at and understand written words; or to interpret information from signs, data, or other sources.
examples: I read a chapter before bed.
Can you read the sign from here?
entries.tip: The spelling stays the same, but the past tense “read” is pronounced /red/, like “red”.
entries.breakdown: Usually means understanding written language, but can also mean interpreting signals, expressions, or data.

senses.definition: To look at written or printed words and understand their meaning.
senses.definitionZh: 查看书写或印刷的文字并理解其含义。
examples: She reads a book every week.
I read the instructions before using the machine.

senses.definition: To understand or interpret information shown by signs, numbers, expressions, or other clues.
senses.definitionZh: 理解或解读标志、数字、表情或其他线索所传达的信息。
examples: The device can read a barcode.
He could read the worry on her face.

senses.definition: A piece of writing or a book that someone reads, especially when describing how enjoyable or interesting it is.
senses.definitionZh: 供人阅读的文章或书籍，尤指用来评价其趣味性或可读性。
examples: The article is an easy read.
That novel is a fascinating read.

entries.definition: A place where goods are sold; or to visit stores to look at or buy things.
examples: There is a small shop near the station.
We usually shop for groceries on Saturday.
entries.tip: “Shop” is common in British English; “store” is more common in American English for many types of retail business.
entries.breakdown: The noun is a place that sells goods; the verb describes visiting places to buy or browse.

senses.definition: A place where goods are sold to customers.
senses.definitionZh: 向顾客出售商品的地方；商店。
examples: The bookshop closes at six.
I bought some fruit at the local shop.

senses.definition: To visit shops or websites to look for or buy goods.
senses.definitionZh: 前往商店或网站寻找、挑选或购买商品；购物。
examples: We shop online when we are busy.
She shops for clothes twice a year.

entries.definition: To move over a surface on skates with wheels or blades; or a boot or shoe fitted with them.
entries.definitionZh: 滑冰；滑旱冰；冰鞋；轮滑鞋
examples: The children skate at the rink after school.
He learned to skate on the frozen lake.
entries.tip: “Ice-skate” specifies skating on ice; “roller-skate” uses wheeled skates.
entries.breakdown: Usually refers to moving while wearing footwear designed to glide over ice or a smooth surface.

senses.definition: To move across ice or another smooth surface while wearing skates.
senses.definitionZh: 穿着冰鞋或轮滑鞋在冰面或其他平滑表面上滑行。
examples: She skates confidently on the ice.
We went to the park to roller-skate.

senses.definition: A boot or shoe fitted with a blade or wheels for skating.
senses.definitionZh: 装有冰刀或轮子的滑行靴或鞋；冰鞋或轮滑鞋。
examples: He bought a new pair of skates.
Make sure your skates fit properly.

entries.definition: A long, narrow piece of equipment attached to a boot for travelling over snow; or to move over snow using skis.
entries.definitionZh: 滑雪板；滑雪；进行滑雪运动
examples: She learned to ski when she was young.
He bought a new pair of skis.
entries.tip: The plural is “skis”; the activity is often called skiing.
entries.breakdown: Can refer to the equipment or the activity of travelling over snow on it.

senses.definition: One of a pair of long, narrow pieces of equipment used to move over snow.
senses.definitionZh: 用于在雪地上移动的一对细长装备之一；滑雪板。
examples: One ski was damaged during the trip.
She rented skis at the resort.

senses.definition: To travel over snow while standing on skis.
senses.definitionZh: 站在滑雪板上在雪地上滑行；滑雪。
examples: They ski every winter.
We skied down a gentle slope.

entries.definition: The natural state of rest in which the body and mind are less active; or to be in that state.
examples: I need more sleep during the week.
The baby is sleeping upstairs.
entries.tip: The past tense and past participle are “slept”. Common phrases include go to sleep and fall asleep.
entries.breakdown: Refers to the resting state or the act of being in that state; it is different from “rest”, which does not always involve sleeping.

senses.definition: The natural condition of resting in which a person or animal is usually unconscious and less aware of the surroundings.
senses.definitionZh: 人或动物自然休息的状态，通常处于无意识且对周围环境感知较弱的状态；睡眠。
examples: A good night's sleep helps me concentrate.
The noise interrupted my sleep.

senses.definition: To be in the natural resting state in which the body and mind are less active.
senses.definitionZh: 处于身体和精神活动减弱的自然休息状态；睡觉。
examples: The children sleep for ten hours.
I slept badly because of the heat.

entries.definition: A series of connected railway vehicles that carry passengers or goods; or to teach and practise skills for a particular job or activity.
examples: We took the train to the city.
The company trains new employees.
entries.tip: As a verb, train can mean practise to improve performance or teach someone how to do a job.
entries.breakdown: The noun usually refers to railway transport; the verb refers to developing skills through instruction and practice.

senses.definition: A series of connected railway vehicles pulled by an engine along tracks.
senses.definitionZh: 由机车牵引、沿铁轨行驶的一组连接车辆；火车或列车。
examples: The train arrives at platform three.
We travelled by train across the country.

senses.definition: To practise regularly in order to improve physical ability or performance.
senses.definitionZh: 通过定期练习提高体能或表现。
examples: She trains for a marathon every morning.
The team trains twice a week.

senses.definition: To teach someone the knowledge or skills needed for a job or activity.
senses.definitionZh: 教授某人从事工作或活动所需的知识与技能。
examples: The hotel trains its staff in customer service.
He was trained to operate the equipment.

entries.definition: To form letters, words, or other symbols on a surface or digital device; or to create a text such as a message, letter, or story.
examples: Please write your name at the top of the page.
She writes stories for children.
entries.tip: The past tense and past participle are “wrote” and “written”. “Write down” means record information in writing.
entries.breakdown: Can refer to forming written symbols or creating a longer piece of text.

senses.definition: To make letters, words, or symbols using a pen, pencil, keyboard, or another tool.
senses.definitionZh: 使用笔、铅笔、键盘或其他工具写出字母、单词或符号。
examples: Write the answer in the space provided.
He writes with his left hand.

senses.definition: To create a piece of writing, such as a letter, report, article, or story.
senses.definitionZh: 创作信件、报告、文章或故事等文字作品。
examples: I wrote an email to the manager.
She is writing a book about her travels.
